controls.title: Identity and credential management
controls.summary: Identities and credentials for users, services, and hardware are issued, managed, verified, revoked, and audited. In cloud environments this means every IAM user, role, and access key has a clear owner, least-privilege permissions, and is rotated or removed when no longer needed.
references: NIST CSF 2.0, Protect function, Identity Management and Access Control category

controls.title: Access permissions and authorization
controls.summary: Access permissions, entitlements, and authorizations are defined and enforced following least privilege and separation of duties. Over-permissive cloud IAM policies that grant wildcard actions or administrator access to broad principals violate this control.
references: NIST CSF 2.0, Protect function, Identity Management and Access Control category

controls.title: Data-at-rest protection
controls.summary: The confidentiality and integrity of stored data are protected. For cloud storage this requires server-side or client-side encryption of buckets, disks, and databases using managed or customer-managed keys, so that data on disk is unreadable without authorization.
references: NIST CSF 2.0, Protect function, Data Security category

controls.title: Data-in-transit protection
controls.summary: Data moving across networks is protected in transit. Cloud services must enforce TLS for API and application traffic and disable plaintext protocols, preventing interception of sensitive data between clients and services.
references: NIST CSF 2.0, Protect function, Data Security category

controls.title: Network and environment monitoring
controls.summary: Networks and the operating environment are monitored to detect potential cybersecurity events. In cloud this includes enabling flow logs, audit logs, and configuration-change logging so that anomalous access or changes are recorded and can be investigated.
references: NIST CSF 2.0, Detect function, Continuous Monitoring category

controls.title: Network segmentation and boundary protection
controls.summary: Networks are segmented and protected at their boundaries. Security groups, firewalls, and network ACLs should restrict inbound access to only required ports and sources; exposing administrative ports such as SSH or RDP to the entire internet violates this control.
references: NIST CSF 2.0, Protect function, Technology Infrastructure Resilience category
